sentences.text: Mesadactylus is an extinct pterosaur genus found in the Upper Jurassic Morrison Formation of Colorado, United States.

The holotype specimen, BYU 2024 — the specimen the species is based on — consists of a synsacrum made of seven fused sacral vertebrae with a unique complete fusion of spinae into a supraneural blade, alongside associated arm bones, pectoral girdle bones, vertebrae, and femora.
Its holotype features a synsacrum with a unique complete fusion of spinae into a supraneural blade, a structure not seen in other known pterosaurs.
Further study revealed additional material, including a partial braincase, described in 2004 and 2006.
The genus Mesadactylus was named in 1989 by James Jensen and Kevin Padian, with the type species being Mesadactylus ornithosphyos.
Jensen and Padian originally classified Mesadactylus as a pterodactyloid.
However, some sources question whether Mesadactylus belongs to the family Anurognathidae.
Mesadactylus lived during the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages, between 152.21 and 145.06 million years ago.

In 2007, S. Christopher Bennett claimed that the holotype and referred material came from different forms, arguing the synsacrum belonged to an Anurognathidae member while the rest was pterodactyloid.
